docs.title: Compose DND
docs.text:
A library that allows you to easily add drag and drop functionality to your Jetpack Compose or Compose Multiplatform projects.

Try the live demo in your browser.

docs.title: What You Can Build
docs.text:
Every clip is a screen of the sample app. Click one to open its guide.

Drag and drop Reorder a list Drag handle Move between lists Auto scroll Scroll across columns Drag to select Free-form placement Copy on drop Conditional drop Drop strategies Axis lock

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Drag and Drop -- Drag items from one location and drop them onto designated targets.
  • Reorder Lists -- Reorder items within a list using drag and drop gestures.
  • Drag Lifecycle Callbacks -- onDragStart and onDragEnd on every draggable item, a good place to persist state once per drag.
  • Drag to Select / Multi-Select -- Extend a selection by dragging across items, then drag the whole selection as a group.
  • Free-Form Placement -- Drop items anywhere on a board, with the drop animation landing exactly where they snap.
  • Auto Scroll -- Automatically scroll containers, including staggered grids, when dragging items near edges.
  • Drop Strategies -- Choose from multiple built-in strategies to determine which drop target receives the dragged item.
  • Drag Handle -- Restrict the drag gesture to a specific handle area within the item.
  • Axis Lock -- Constrain dragging to the horizontal or vertical axis.
  • Conditional Drop -- Control which drop targets accept which dragged items.
  • Drop Animation -- Smooth spring-based animations when items are dropped.
  • Custom Drag Shadow -- Provide a custom composable to display while an item is being dragged.
  • Enable/Disable -- Toggle drag and drop at the container level or per item.

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
Add the dependency to your module build.gradle.kts:

implementation("com.mohamedrejeb.dnd:compose-dnd:1.0.0-alpha02")

Then use it in your Composable:

val dragAndDropState = rememberDragAndDropState<String>()

DragAndDropContainer(
    state = dragAndDropState,
) {
    val isDragging = dragAndDropState.isDragging("item-1")

    Text(
        text = "Drag me",
        modifier = Modifier
            .graphicsLayer { alpha = if (isDragging) 0f else 1f }
            .draggableItem(
                key = "item-1",
                data = "Hello",
                state = dragAndDropState,
                draggableContent = {
                    Text("Drag me") // Shown as the drag shadow
                },
            ),
    )

    Box(
        modifier = Modifier
            .dropTarget(
                key = "target-1",
                state = dragAndDropState,
                onDrop = { state ->
                    println("Dropped: ${state.data}")
                },
            )
    ) {
        Text("Drop here")
    }
}

For more details, see the Drag and Drop Overview or check out the sample project.

Upgrading from 0.5.0?

1.0.0-alpha02 deprecates ReorderState, rememberReorderState, and ReorderContainer in favor of DragAndDropState everywhere. See the migration guide.

docs.title: Migrating to 1.0
docs.text:
1.0.0-alpha01 unifies the API around a single DragAndDropState and removes the last experimental opt-ins. Nothing was removed outright -- the old reorder wrapper API still compiles, marked @Deprecated, so you can migrate at your own pace module by module.

Tip

Most deprecated symbols carry a replaceWith, so much of this migration is "apply the quick fix" in IntelliJ / Android Studio (Alt+Enter -> Replace with...) rather than hand-editing.

docs.title: ReorderState to DragAndDropState
docs.text:
ReorderState, rememberReorderState, ReorderContainer, and the ReorderableItem(state: ReorderState, ...) overload are deprecated. Reorder with the same DragAndDropState and DragAndDropContainer used for plain drag and drop -- there is now only one state type in the whole library.

Before:

val reorderState = rememberReorderState<String>()

ReorderContainer(
    state = reorderState,
) {
    LazyColumn {
        items(items, key = { it }) { item ->
            ReorderableItem(
                state = reorderState,
                key = item,
                data = item,
                onDragEnter = { state ->
                    items = items.toMutableList().apply {
                        val index = indexOf(item)
                        if (index == -1) return@ReorderableItem
                        remove(state.data)
                        add(index, state.data)
                    }
                },
            ) {
                Text(item)
            }
        }
    }
}

After:

val dndState = rememberDragAndDropState<String>()

DragAndDropContainer(
    state = dndState,
) {
    LazyColumn {
        items(items, key = { it }) { item ->
            ReorderableItem(
                state = dndState,
                key = item,
                data = item,
                onDragEnter = { state ->
                    items = items.toMutableList().apply {
                        val index = indexOf(item)
                        if (index == -1) return@ReorderableItem
                        remove(state.data)
                        add(index, state.data)
                    }
                },
            ) {
                Text(item)
            }
        }
    }
}

If you were using the reorderableItem modifier rather than the ReorderableItem composable, nothing changes -- it already takes a DragAndDropState and was never affected by this deprecation.

If your code read reorderState.dndState to pass the underlying state to a modifier like dragAutoScroll, just pass dndState directly now -- there is no wrapper to unwrap.

docs.title: isDragging: Drop the Import
docs.text:
DragAndDropState.isDragging(key) is now a member function. The old top-level extension in com.mohamedrejeb.compose.dnd.drag is deprecated; a member function of the same name and signature shadows it, so existing calls keep compiling and resolve to the member automatically. The only cleanup needed is removing the now-unused import.

Before:

import com.mohamedrejeb.compose.dnd.drag.isDragging

val isDragging = dragAndDropState.isDragging("item-1")

After:

// no import needed

val isDragging = dragAndDropState.isDragging("item-1")

While you're there, consider isDropTargetHovered(key), the new equivalent of hoveredDropTargetKey == key:

// Before
val isHovered = dragAndDropState.hoveredDropTargetKey == "target-1"

// After
val isHovered = dragAndDropState.isDropTargetHovered("target-1")

docs.title: ExperimentalDndApi: Opt-Ins Are Gone
docs.text:
dragAutoScroll and dragScrollPin are no longer annotated @ExperimentalDndApi, and nothing in the public API requires opt-in anymore. (Axis lock and canDrop never required it, even though older docs said so.) Remove the annotation and the import if nothing else in your file still needs it.

Before:

import com.mohamedrejeb.compose.dnd.annotation.ExperimentalDndApi

@OptIn(ExperimentalDndApi::class)
@Composable
fun ReorderableGrid() {
    val dndState = rememberDragAndDropState<String>()
    val lazyGridState = rememberLazyGridState()

    LazyVerticalGrid(
        modifier = Modifier.dragAutoScroll(
            state = dndState,
            lazyGridState = lazyGridState,
        ),
    ) {
        // ...
    }
}

After:

@Composable
fun ReorderableGrid() {
    val dndState = rememberDragAndDropState<String>()
    val lazyGridState = rememberLazyGridState()

    LazyVerticalGrid(
        modifier = Modifier.dragAutoScroll(
            state = dndState,
            lazyGridState = lazyGridState,
        ),
    ) {
        // ...
    }
}

ExperimentalDndApi itself still exists in the library for now, in case a future API needs it, but nothing currently uses it.

docs.title: DragAutoScrollConfig: maxScrollSpeed Is Now a Dp
docs.text:
maxScrollSpeed used to be a Float in pixels per second, which meant the same config scrolled at different physical speeds on different screen densities. It is now a Dp, so it feels the same everywhere.

Before:

val config = DragAutoScrollConfig(
    minScrollThreshold = 48.dp,
    maxScrollThreshold = 160.dp,
    maxScrollSpeed = 1500f, // px/s
)

After:

val config = DragAutoScrollConfig(
    minScrollThreshold = 48.dp,
    maxScrollThreshold = 160.dp,
    maxScrollSpeed = 600.dp, // dp/s -- the new default
)

If you can't convert your tuned pixel value to Dp right away, a deprecated factory overload accepting maxScrollSpeed: Float is kept for migration -- it behaves exactly as before, so it's a safe stopgap while you pick a good Dp value.

docs.title: DragAutoScrollConfig Is No Longer a data class
docs.text:
DragAutoScrollConfig is a regular class now (its internals need a bit more than a data class' generated methods can offer), but it still exposes a copy() function with the same parameter names (maxScrollSpeed is a Dp there too). The only thing that breaks is destructuring with componentN(), such as val (a, b, c) = config -- use named properties or copy() instead.

Before:

val (minThreshold, maxThreshold, speed) = config
val faster = config.copy(maxScrollSpeed = speed * 1.5f)

After:

val minThreshold = config.minScrollThreshold
val maxThreshold = config.maxScrollThreshold
val speed = config.maxScrollSpeed

val faster = config.copy(maxScrollSpeed = config.maxScrollSpeed * 1.5f)

copy() keeps its shape, so code that builds a config from a base one is unaffected unless it passes maxScrollSpeed as a Float.

docs.title: DraggableItem and ReorderableItem: Parameter Order
docs.text:
The DraggableItem and ReorderableItem composables now start with key, data, state, modifier, the same order as the draggableItem and reorderableItem modifiers. ReorderableItem also takes zIndex after dragAxis.

Calls using named arguments compile unchanged. Only calls passing these arguments positionally need to change:

=== "Before"

```kotlin
ReorderableItem(Modifier.fillMaxWidth(), dndState, item.id, item) {
    ItemRow(item)
}
```

=== "After"

```kotlin
ReorderableItem(
    key = item.id,
    data = item,
    state = dndState,
    modifier = Modifier.fillMaxWidth(),
) {
    ItemRow(item)
}
```

docs.title: DropStrategy: SurfacePercentage and the Default
docs.text:
DropStrategy.SurfacePercentage used to divide the overlap by the dragged item's area. That value is the same for every target, so it always picked the same target as DropStrategy.Surface. It now divides by each drop target's own area: the target covered the most, as a share of its size, wins.

The default dropStrategy changed from SurfacePercentage to Surface, so items relying on the default hover exactly as before.

You only need to act if you pass dropStrategy = DropStrategy.SurfacePercentage explicitly and your drop targets have different sizes: switch to DropStrategy.Surface to keep the old behavior.

docs.title: What's New (Not a Breaking Change)
docs.text:
These are additive and don't require any changes to existing code:

  • DragAndDropState.cancelDrag() to abort a drag programmatically -- see Overview: Cancelling a Drag Programmatically.
  • onDragStart / onDragEnd callbacks on every draggable item -- see Overview: Drag Lifecycle.
  • canDrop on reorderableItem / ReorderableItem, for pinned or locked rows -- see Reorder List: Pinned or Locked Items.
  • dragAutoScroll / dragScrollPin overloads for LazyStaggeredGridState -- see Auto Scroll.
  • New Drag to Select and Multi-Select and Free-Form Placement guides.

See the CHANGELOG for the full list of changes in 1.0.0-alpha01.

docs.title: Auto Scroll
docs.text: When dragging items in a scrollable container, you often need the container to scroll automatically as the user drags near its edges. Compose DND provides the dragAutoScroll modifier for this purpose.

docs.title: LazyColumn / LazyRow
docs.text:
Use the dragAutoScroll modifier on a LazyColumn or LazyRow to enable automatic scrolling during drag operations:

@Composable
fun AutoScrollLazyColumnExample() {
    val dndState = rememberDragAndDropState<String>()
    val lazyListState = rememberLazyListState()

    DragAndDropContainer(
        state = dndState,
    ) {
        LazyColumn(
            state = lazyListState,
            modifier = Modifier
                .fillMaxSize()
                .dragAutoScroll(
                    state = dndState,
                    lazyListState = lazyListState,
                ),
        ) {
            // items...
        }
    }
}

docs.title: LazyGrid
docs.text:
For LazyVerticalGrid or LazyHorizontalGrid, use the grid variant:

@Composable
fun AutoScrollLazyGridExample() {
    val dndState = rememberDragAndDropState<String>()
    val lazyGridState = rememberLazyGridState()

    DragAndDropContainer(
        state = dndState,
    ) {
        LazyVerticalGrid(
            columns = GridCells.Fixed(3),
            state = lazyGridState,
            modifier = Modifier
                .fillMaxSize()
                .dragAutoScroll(
                    state = dndState,
                    lazyGridState = lazyGridState,
                ),
        ) {
            // items...
        }
    }
}

docs.title: LazyVerticalStaggeredGrid / LazyHorizontalStaggeredGrid
docs.text:
For a masonry-style staggered grid, use the lazyStaggeredGridState overload:

@Composable
fun AutoScrollStaggeredGridExample() {
    val dndState = rememberDragAndDropState<String>()
    val staggeredGridState = rememberLazyStaggeredGridState()

    DragAndDropContainer(
        state = dndState,
    ) {
        LazyVerticalStaggeredGrid(
            columns = StaggeredGridCells.Fixed(2),
            state = staggeredGridState,
            modifier = Modifier
                .fillMaxSize()
                .dragAutoScroll(
                    state = dndState,
                    lazyStaggeredGridState = staggeredGridState,
                ),
        ) {
            // items...
        }
    }
}

docs.title: ScrollState (Column / Row)
docs.text:
For regular scrollable containers using ScrollState, pass the orientation parameter:

@Composable
fun AutoScrollColumnExample() {
    val dndState = rememberDragAndDropState<String>()
    val scrollState = rememberScrollState()

    DragAndDropContainer(
        state = dndState,
    ) {
        Column(
            modifier = Modifier
                .fillMaxSize()
                .verticalScroll(scrollState)
                .dragAutoScroll(
                    state = dndState,
                    scrollState = scrollState,
                    orientation = Orientation.Vertical,
                ),
        ) {
            // items...
        }
    }
}

docs.title: Reversed and Right-to-Left Layouts
docs.text:
Auto scroll follows the layout: a lazy list or grid with reverseLayout = true, and any horizontal layout in a right-to-left locale, scrolls toward the edge the dragged item is held at.

Two cases are not supported yet: a staggered grid with reverseLayout = true, and a ScrollState used with reverseScrolling = true.

docs.title: DragAutoScrollConfig
docs.text:
You can customize the auto scroll behavior using DragAutoScrollConfig:

val config = DragAutoScrollConfig(
    minScrollThreshold = 48.dp,
    maxScrollThreshold = 160.dp,
    maxScrollSpeed = 600.dp,
)

LazyColumn(
    state = lazyListState,
    modifier = Modifier
        .fillMaxSize()
        .dragAutoScroll(
            state = dndState,
            lazyListState = lazyListState,
            config = config,
        ),
)

docs.title: Configuration Options
docs.text:
Parameter Type Default Description minScrollThreshold Dp DragAutoScrollConfig.DefaultMinScrollThreshold (48.dp) Minimum distance from the edge where scrolling begins. The effective threshold adapts to the first/last visible item size: clamp(itemSize, minScrollThreshold, maxScrollThreshold), and never more than a quarter of the viewport. maxScrollThreshold Dp DragAutoScrollConfig.DefaultMaxScrollThreshold (160.dp) Maximum distance from the edge for auto-scroll activation. Prevents the adaptive threshold from growing too large with tall items or containers. maxScrollSpeed Dp DragAutoScrollConfig.DefaultMaxScrollSpeed (600.dp) The maximum scroll speed, as a distance scrolled per second at the very edge. Being a Dp, the scroll feels the same on every screen density.

DragAutoScrollConfig is a regular class, not a data class, but it still exposes copy():

val fasterConfig = DragAutoScrollConfig().copy(maxScrollSpeed = 900.dp)

maxScrollSpeed used to be a Float

Before 1.0.0-alpha01, maxScrollSpeed was a Float in pixels per second, which scrolled at different physical speeds on different screen densities. It is now a Dp. A deprecated factory taking maxScrollSpeed: Float is kept for migration -- see the migration guide.

docs.title: How It Works
docs.text:
The auto scroll mechanism uses a dynamic threshold approach:

  1. Detection -- When an edge of the dragged item is within the scroll threshold distance from the container edge, scrolling begins.
  2. Large items follow the pointer -- An item too large to fit between the two edge zones (a Kanban column on a phone) would touch both all the time. Its edges are followed no further from the pointer than half the free space, so for large items the pointer decides when to scroll.
  3. No scroll on pick-up -- An item picked up next to an edge doesn't scroll the list under your finger. It starts scrolling once the pointer moves toward that edge by 8.dp, or once the item leaves the edge zone and comes back.
  4. Quadratic Easing -- Scroll speed increases quadratically as the dragged item moves closer to the edge. This provides a natural feel where small movements near the threshold produce slow scrolling, while pushing toward the edge accelerates.
  5. Frame-Synced -- Scroll operations are synchronized with the frame rate for smooth, jank-free scrolling.
  6. Bidirectional -- Scrolling works in both directions: toward the start and toward the end of the container.
  7. Bounded -- Auto-scroll stays idle once the container can't scroll further in that direction, instead of spinning frames against the end of the list.

docs.title: Scroll Pinning (dragScrollPin)
docs.text:
When reorderable items have different sizes, swapping two items changes the content size above the viewport. Compose's key-based scroll anchoring then adjusts the scroll position to compensate, which shows up as a visible jump during the drag.

The dragScrollPin modifier fixes this by pinning the scroll position right before each reorder swap, so the viewport stays stable:

@Composable
fun ScrollPinExample() {
    val dndState = rememberDragAndDropState<String>()
    val lazyListState = rememberLazyListState()

    DragAndDropContainer(
        state = dndState,
    ) {
        LazyColumn(
            state = lazyListState,
            modifier = Modifier
                .fillMaxSize()
                .dragScrollPin(
                    state = dndState,
                    lazyListState = lazyListState,
                ),
        ) {
            // items with varying heights...
        }
    }
}

lazyGridState and lazyStaggeredGridState overloads are available for LazyVerticalGrid / LazyHorizontalGrid and LazyVerticalStaggeredGrid / LazyHorizontalStaggeredGrid.

Note

dragAutoScroll already includes the scroll pinning behavior, so you do not need both. Use dragScrollPin on its own only when you want jump-free reordering without automatic edge scrolling.

docs.title: Full Working Example
docs.text:
@Composable
fun ReorderWithAutoScroll() {
    val dndState = rememberDragAndDropState<String>()
    var items by remember {
        mutableStateOf(
            (1..50).map { "Item $it" }
        )
    }
    val lazyListState = rememberLazyListState()

    DragAndDropContainer(
        state = dndState,
        modifier = Modifier.fillMaxSize().padding(16.dp),
    ) {
        LazyColumn(
            state = lazyListState,
            verticalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(8.dp),
            modifier = Modifier
                .fillMaxSize()
                .dragAutoScroll(
                    state = dndState,
                    lazyListState = lazyListState,
                ),
        ) {
            items(items, key = { it }) { item ->
                val isDragging = dndState.isDragging(item)

                ItemCard(
                    text = item,
                    modifier = Modifier
                        .graphicsLayer {
                            alpha = if (isDragging) 0f else 1f
                        }
                        .reorderableItem(
                            key = item,
                            data = item,
                            state = dndState,
                            onDragEnter = { state ->
                                items = items.toMutableList().apply {
                                    val index = indexOf(item)
                                    if (index != -1) {
                                        remove(state.data)
                                        add(index, state.data)
                                    }
                                }
                            },
                            draggableContent = {
                                ItemCard(text = item)
                            },
                        )
                        .fillMaxWidth(),
                )
            }
        }
    }
}

@Composable
private fun ItemCard(
    text: String,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
) {
    Card(
        modifier = modifier.height(56.dp),
    ) {
        Box(
            contentAlignment = Alignment.CenterStart,
            modifier = Modifier
                .fillMaxSize()
                .padding(horizontal = 16.dp),
        ) {
            Text(text = text)
        }
    }
}

docs.title: Axis Lock
docs.text: By default, items can be dragged freely in any direction. Axis lock constrains the drag movement to a single axis -- either horizontal or vertical. This is useful for lists, sliders, or any UI where dragging should only occur along one dimension.

docs.title: DragAxis
docs.text:
The DragAxis enum defines the available axis constraints:

Value Description Free Item can be dragged in any direction (default). Horizontal Item can only be dragged along the horizontal axis. Vertical Item can only be dragged along the vertical axis.

docs.title: Usage with draggableItem
docs.text:
val isDragging = dragAndDropState.isDragging("item-1")

Text(
    text = "I can only move up and down",
    modifier = Modifier
        .graphicsLayer {
            alpha = if (isDragging) 0f else 1f
        }
        .draggableItem(
            key = "item-1",
            data = "Hello",
            state = dragAndDropState,
            dragAxis = DragAxis.Vertical,
            draggableContent = {
                Text(text = "I can only move up and down")
            },
        ),
)

docs.title: Usage with reorderableItem
docs.text:
Axis lock works naturally with reorderable lists. For a vertical list, lock to the vertical axis so items cannot be dragged sideways:

@Composable
fun VerticalLockedReorderExample() {
    val dndState = rememberDragAndDropState<String>()
    var items by remember {
        mutableStateOf(listOf("Item 1", "Item 2", "Item 3", "Item 4"))
    }

    DragAndDropContainer(
        state = dndState,
    ) {
        LazyColumn(
            verticalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(8.dp),
            modifier = Modifier.fillMaxSize().padding(16.dp),
        ) {
            items(items, key = { it }) { item ->
                val isDragging = dndState.isDragging(item)

                ItemCard(
                    text = item,
                    modifier = Modifier
                        .graphicsLayer {
                            alpha = if (isDragging) 0f else 1f
                        }
                        .reorderableItem(
                            key = item,
                            data = item,
                            state = dndState,
                            dragAxis = DragAxis.Vertical,
                            onDragEnter = { state ->
                                items = items.toMutableList().apply {
                                    val index = indexOf(item)
                                    if (index != -1) {
                                        remove(state.data)
                                        add(index, state.data)
                                    }
                                }
                            },
                            draggableContent = {
                                ItemCard(text = item)
                            },
                        )
                        .fillMaxWidth(),
                )
            }
        }
    }
}

@Composable
private fun ItemCard(
    text: String,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
) {
    Card(
        modifier = modifier.height(56.dp),
    ) {
        Box(
            contentAlignment = Alignment.CenterStart,
            modifier = Modifier
                .fillMaxSize()
                .padding(horizontal = 16.dp),
        ) {
            Text(text = text)
        }
    }
}

docs.title: Horizontal Axis Lock
docs.text:
For a horizontal list or row:

ItemCard(
    text = item,
    modifier = Modifier.reorderableItem(
        key = item,
        data = item,
        state = dndState,
        dragAxis = DragAxis.Horizontal,
        onDragEnter = { /* reorder logic */ },
        draggableContent = {
            ItemCard(text = item)
        },
    ),
)

docs.title: How It Works
docs.text:
When axis lock is active:

  • Vertical -- The drag shadow moves only along the Y axis. Any horizontal movement from the pointer is ignored, keeping the item aligned in its column.
  • Horizontal -- The drag shadow moves only along the X axis. Any vertical movement is ignored.
  • Free -- Both axes are tracked, allowing unconstrained dragging.

Tip

Axis lock is particularly useful combined with auto scroll. For vertical lists, locking to DragAxis.Vertical ensures the drag shadow stays aligned with the list while auto scroll handles navigation.

docs.title: Conditional Drop
docs.text: By default, any dragged item can be dropped on any drop target. Conditional drop lets you control which drop targets accept which items, enabling scenarios such as typed drop zones, capacity limits, or permission-based dropping.

docs.title: Using canDrop
docs.text:
The canDrop parameter on the dropTarget modifier is a plain Boolean, evaluated by Compose like any other modifier argument. Because it is just a boolean expression, it can read live state -- including state.draggedItem?.data -- to accept or reject whichever item is currently being dragged:

Box(
    modifier = Modifier
        .dropTarget(
            key = "numbers-only",
            state = dragAndDropState,
            // Only accept items whose data is a number
            canDrop = dragAndDropState.draggedItem?.data is Int,
            onDrop = { state ->
                println("Accepted: ${state.data}")
            },
        )
) {
    Text("Numbers only")
}

When canDrop is false, the target is excluded from hover detection entirely: it will not trigger onDragEnter, onDragExit, or onDrop for that item, and hoveredDropTargetKey never points to it.

docs.title: Typed Drop Zones
docs.text:
Accept only specific data types in different zones:

@Composable
fun TypedDropZonesExample() {
    val dragAndDropState = rememberDragAndDropState<Any>()
    val draggedData = dragAndDropState.draggedItem?.data

    DragAndDropContainer(state = dragAndDropState) {
        Row(
            horizontalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(16.dp),
            modifier = Modifier.fillMaxWidth(),
        ) {
            // Only accepts strings
            Box(
                modifier = Modifier
                    .weight(1f)
                    .height(200.dp)
                    .dropTarget(
                        key = "text-zone",
                        state = dragAndDropState,
                        canDrop = draggedData is String,
                        onDrop = { /* handle text drop */ },
                    )
            ) {
                Text("Text Zone")
            }

            // Only accepts integers
            Box(
                modifier = Modifier
                    .weight(1f)
                    .height(200.dp)
                    .dropTarget(
                        key = "number-zone",
                        state = dragAndDropState,
                        canDrop = draggedData is Int,
                        onDrop = { /* handle number drop */ },
                    )
            ) {
                Text("Number Zone")
            }
        }
    }
}

docs.title: Capacity Limits
docs.text:
Prevent dropping when a zone is full:

val maxItems = 5
var droppedItems by remember { mutableStateOf(listOf<String>()) }

Box(
    modifier = Modifier
        .dropTarget(
            key = "limited-zone",
            state = dragAndDropState,
            canDrop = droppedItems.size < maxItems,
            onDrop = { state ->
                droppedItems = droppedItems + state.data
            },
        )
) {
    Text("${droppedItems.size} / $maxItems")
}

docs.title: Preventing Self-Drop
docs.text:
Prevent an item from being dropped back onto itself:

Box(
    modifier = Modifier
        .dropTarget(
            key = item.id,
            state = dragAndDropState,
            canDrop = dragAndDropState.draggedItem?.key != item.id,
            onDrop = { state ->
                // Handle drop from a different item
            },
        )
)

docs.title: Interaction with dropTargets Parameter
docs.text:
The canDrop parameter on the drop target is different from the dropTargets parameter on the draggableItem modifier:

Feature dropTargets (on draggableItem) canDrop (on dropTarget) Defined on The dragged item The drop target Filters by Drop target keys (allowlist) Custom boolean expression on live state Use case "This item can only go to zones A, B" "This zone only accepts certain items"

Both can be combined. The dragged item first checks its dropTargets list, and then the drop target checks its canDrop value.

docs.title: Visual Feedback
docs.text:
Combine canDrop with isDropTargetHovered to provide visual feedback:

@Composable
fun ConditionalDropWithFeedback() {
    val dragAndDropState = rememberDragAndDropState<String>()
    val isHovered = dragAndDropState.isDropTargetHovered("target-1")
    val draggedText = dragAndDropState.draggedItem?.data

    Box(
        modifier = Modifier
            .border(
                width = 2.dp,
                color = if (isHovered) Color.Green else Color.Gray,
            )
            .dropTarget(
                key = "target-1",
                state = dragAndDropState,
                // Only accept short strings
                canDrop = draggedText == null || draggedText.length <= 10,
                onDrop = { state ->
                    println("Dropped: ${state.data}")
                },
            )
    ) {
        Text("Short strings only")
    }
}

Note

When canDrop is false, the drop target will not trigger onDragEnter, onDragExit, or onDrop for that item. hoveredDropTargetKey will not be set to this target's key, so visual hover feedback will not activate either.

Tip

reorderableItem and ReorderableItem have their own canDrop parameter for keeping specific rows out of a reorder -- for example pinned or locked items. See Reorder List: Pinned or Locked Items.

docs.title: Drag Handle
docs.text: By default, dragging can be initiated from anywhere within a draggable item. A drag handle restricts the drag gesture to a specific area within the item, such as a grip icon. This is useful when your item contains interactive elements like buttons or text fields that should not trigger a drag.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Two pieces work together:

  1. Pass hasDragHandle = true to the draggableItem or reorderableItem modifier - this stops the item body from initiating drags.
  2. Apply Modifier.dragHandle(key, state) to the composable that should act as the handle, using the same key as the item.
Row(
    modifier = Modifier
        .reorderableItem(
            key = item,
            data = item,
            state = dndState,
            hasDragHandle = true,
            onDragEnter = { /* reorder */ },
            draggableContent = { ItemRow(item) },
        ),
) {
    Icon(
        imageVector = Icons.Rounded.DragHandle,
        contentDescription = "Drag handle",
        modifier = Modifier.dragHandle(
            key = item,
            state = dndState,
        ), // only this area initiates drag
    )
    Text(item) // the rest of the item stays interactive
}

docs.title: dragHandle Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Default Description key Any Required The key of the draggable item this handle controls. state DragAndDropState<T> Required The drag and drop state. enabled Boolean true Whether the drag handle is active. dragAfterLongPress Boolean false If true, drag starts after a long press on the handle. requireFirstDownUnconsumed Boolean false If true, the first down event on the handle must be unconsumed.

docs.title: Full Example: Reorderable List with Handles
docs.text:
@Composable
fun DragHandleExample() {
    val dndState = rememberDragAndDropState<String>()
    var items by remember {
        mutableStateOf(listOf("Item 1", "Item 2", "Item 3"))
    }

    DragAndDropContainer(
        state = dndState,
    ) {
        LazyColumn(
            verticalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(8.dp),
            modifier = Modifier.fillMaxSize().padding(16.dp),
        ) {
            items(items, key = { it }) { item ->
                val isDragging = dndState.isDragging(item)

                Row(
                    verticalAlignment = Alignment.CenterVertically,
                    modifier = Modifier
                        .graphicsLayer {
                            alpha = if (isDragging) 0f else 1f
                        }
                        .reorderableItem(
                            key = item,
                            data = item,
                            state = dndState,
                            hasDragHandle = true,
                            onDragEnter = { state ->
                                items = items.toMutableList().apply {
                                    val index = indexOf(item)
                                    if (index != -1) {
                                        remove(state.data)
                                        add(index, state.data)
                                    }
                                }
                            },
                            draggableContent = {
                                HandleRow(text = item)
                            },
                        )
                        .fillMaxWidth()
                        .height(56.dp)
                        .padding(horizontal = 16.dp),
                ) {
                    // Only this area initiates the drag
                    Icon(
                        imageVector = Icons.Rounded.DragHandle,
                        contentDescription = "Drag handle",
                        modifier = Modifier.dragHandle(
                            key = item,
                            state = dndState,
                        ),
                    )

                    Spacer(modifier = Modifier.width(16.dp))

                    Text(text = item)
                }
            }
        }
    }
}

docs.title: With the Wrapper Composables
docs.text:
Inside DraggableItem or ReorderableItem content, the scope provides a Modifier.dragHandle() overload that needs no key or state - and no hasDragHandle flag, since calling it marks the item automatically:

ReorderableItem(state = dndState, key = item, data = item) {
    Row {
        Icon(
            imageVector = Icons.Rounded.DragHandle,
            contentDescription = "Drag handle",
            modifier = Modifier.dragHandle(), // scope version
        )
        Text(item)
    }
}

The scope overload accepts the same enabled, dragAfterLongPress, and requireFirstDownUnconsumed parameters.

docs.title: How It Works
docs.text:
When an item has a drag handle:

  • Touch events on the item body are not intercepted for drag gestures.
  • Only touch events starting inside the handle area will initiate a drag.
  • Other interactive elements (buttons, text fields, checkboxes) inside the item remain fully functional.

Tip

Drag handles are especially useful in reorderable lists where each item contains clickable elements. Without a drag handle, tapping a button might accidentally start a drag gesture.

docs.title: Drop Strategies
docs.text: When a dragged item overlaps multiple drop targets, a drop strategy determines which target is considered "hovered." Compose DND provides several built-in strategies and allows you to create custom ones.

docs.title: What Are Drop Strategies?
docs.text: During a drag operation, the dragged item may visually overlap more than one drop target at the same time. The drop strategy is the algorithm that decides which single drop target should receive the onDragEnter, onDragExit, and onDrop callbacks.

docs.title: Surface (Default)
docs.text:
Selects the drop target with the largest absolute overlapping area (in pixels) with the dragged item, regardless of the target's own size. This is the default strategy and works well for most use cases.

Text(
    text = "Hello",
    modifier = Modifier.draggableItem(
        key = "item-1",
        data = "Hello",
        state = dragAndDropState,
        dropStrategy = DropStrategy.Surface,
        draggableContent = {
            Text(text = "Hello")
        },
    ),
)

docs.title: SurfacePercentage
docs.text:
Selects the drop target that has the highest percentage of its own surface covered by the dragged item.

Text(
    text = "Hello",
    modifier = Modifier.draggableItem(
        key = "item-1",
        data = "Hello",
        state = dragAndDropState,
        dropStrategy = DropStrategy.SurfacePercentage,
        draggableContent = {
            Text(text = "Hello")
        },
    ),
)

The percentage is calculated as:

overlapping area / drop target area

This means a smaller drop target that is fully covered by the dragged item is preferred over a larger target that is only partially covered. When all targets have the same size, it picks the same target as Surface.

docs.title: CenterDistance
docs.text:
Selects the drop target whose center is closest to the center of the dragged item. This strategy ignores overlap area entirely and focuses on proximity.

Text(
    text = "Hello",
    modifier = Modifier.draggableItem(
        key = "item-1",
        data = "Hello",
        state = dragAndDropState,
        dropStrategy = DropStrategy.CenterDistance,
        draggableContent = {
            Text(text = "Hello")
        },
    ),
)

docs.title: Comparison
docs.text: Strategy Algorithm Best For Surface Max absolute overlapping area General purpose, lists and grids (default) SurfacePercentage Max overlapping area / target area Small targets next to large ones CenterDistance Min distance between centers Precise targeting, small targets

docs.title: Z-Index
docs.text:
All built-in strategies account for the zIndex property of drop targets. When drop targets overlap visually, the one with a higher zIndex takes priority:

Box(
    modifier = Modifier
        .dropTarget(
            key = "background-target",
            state = dragAndDropState,
            zIndex = 0f, // Lower priority
            onDrop = { /* ... */ },
        )
) {
    Box(
        modifier = Modifier
            .dropTarget(
                key = "foreground-target",
                state = dragAndDropState,
                zIndex = 1f, // Higher priority
                onDrop = { /* ... */ },
            )
    )
}

docs.title: Usage with reorderableItem
docs.text:
Drop strategies also work with the reorderableItem modifier:

Card(
    modifier = Modifier.reorderableItem(
        key = item,
        data = item,
        state = dndState,
        dropStrategy = DropStrategy.CenterDistance,
        onDragEnter = { state ->
            // Reorder logic
        },
        draggableContent = {
            // Drag shadow content
        },
    ),
) {
    // ...
}

docs.title: Custom Drop Strategy
docs.text:
You can create a custom drop strategy by implementing the DropStrategy interface:

object MyCustomStrategy : DropStrategy {
    override fun <T> getHoveredDropTarget(
        draggedItemTopLeft: Offset,
        draggedItemSize: Size,
        dropTargets: List<DropTargetState<T>>,
    ): DropTargetState<T>? {
        // Your custom logic here
        return dropTargets.firstOrNull()
    }
}

Then use it:

Text(
    text = "Hello",
    modifier = Modifier.draggableItem(
        key = "item-1",
        data = "Hello",
        state = dragAndDropState,
        dropStrategy = MyCustomStrategy,
        draggableContent = {
            Text(text = "Hello")
        },
    ),
)

docs.title: Form Builder (Copy on Drop)
docs.text:
Most drag and drop moves an item from one place to another. A form builder needs something different: dragging a field type from a palette should create a new field in the form while the palette chip stays put. This guide walks through the pattern used by the Form Builder sample.

The building blocks:

  • A sealed drag payload so palette items and existing form fields share one DragAndDropState.
  • Palette chips as draggableItems whose source is never hidden or removed — a copy is created on drop.
  • Form rows as reorderableItems that insert palette drops at their position and reorder existing fields on hover.
  • An append slot at the end of the form, doubling as the empty-form target.

docs.title: One State, Two Payloads
docs.text:
A DragAndDropState<T> carries one data type, but palette chips and form fields are different things. Model both as a sealed hierarchy:

sealed interface FormDragData {
    data class PaletteItem(val type: FieldType) : FormDragData

    data class ExistingField(val field: FormField) : FormDragData
}

val dndState = rememberDragAndDropState<FormDragData>()

Every drop target can now branch on what was dropped.

docs.title: The Palette: Sources That Stay Put
docs.text:
Each palette chip is a plain draggableItem. Two things distinguish it from a move:

  • The key is stable ("palette-Email") and the chip is never removed from the palette.
  • There is no graphicsLayer { alpha = ... } trick — the source stays visible while its drag shadow flies.
PaletteChipContent(
    type = type,
    modifier = Modifier.draggableItem(
        key = "palette-${type.name}",
        data = FormDragData.PaletteItem(type),
        state = dndState,
        draggableContent = {
            PaletteChipContent(type = type, isDragShadow = true)
        },
    ),
)

docs.title: Insert on Drop, Reorder on Enter
docs.text:
The two payloads want different timing:

  • Existing fields reorder in onDragEnter, like any sortable list — the live displacement is the feedback.
  • Palette items must wait for onDrop. Creating the field in onDragEnter would leave phantom copies behind every row the drag passes over.

Each form row's reorderableItem handles both:

Modifier.reorderableItem(
    key = field.id,
    data = FormDragData.ExistingField(field),
    state = dndState,
    hasDragHandle = true,
    dropStrategy = DropStrategy.CenterDistance,
    onDragEnter = { state ->
        val entered = state.data
        if (entered is FormDragData.ExistingField && entered.field.id != field.id) {
            fields = fields.moveBefore(entered.field, field)
        }
    },
    onDrop = { state ->
        val dropped = state.data
        if (dropped is FormDragData.PaletteItem) {
            val index = fields.indexOfFirst { it.id == field.id }
            if (index != -1) fields = fields.insertAt(index, newField(dropped.type))
        }
    },
    draggableContent = { FormFieldRow(field, isDragShadow = true) },
)

Rows drag by a grip handle (hasDragHandle = true plus Modifier.dragHandle(key, state) on the grip icon), so the delete button and future inputs stay clickable.

docs.title: Showing Where the Field Will Land
docs.text:
Palette drops insert above the hovered row, so mark that edge while a palette item is in the air. isDropTargetHovered plus a type check on draggedItem is all it takes:

val isPaletteItemHovering = dndState.draggedItem?.data is FormDragData.PaletteItem &&
    dndState.isDropTargetHovered(field.id)

The sample tints the hovered row and draws an accent bar across its top edge:

Modifier.drawBehind {
    if (isPaletteItemHovering) {
        drawRoundRect(
            color = accent,
            size = Size(width = size.width, height = 3.dp.toPx()),
            cornerRadius = CornerRadius(1.5.dp.toPx()),
        )
    }
}

docs.title: The Append Slot
docs.text:
A dashed dropTarget after the last row accepts both payloads — palette items append a new field, existing fields move to the end. When the form is empty it grows into the main call-to-action:

Box(
    modifier = Modifier
        .dropTarget(
            key = "append-slot",
            state = dndState,
            dropAnimationEnabled = false,
            onDrop = { state ->
                when (val data = state.data) {
                    is FormDragData.PaletteItem -> fields = fields + newField(data.type)
                    is FormDragData.ExistingField ->
                        fields = fields.filter { it.id != data.field.id } + data.field
                }
            },
        ),
) {
    Text(if (fields.isEmpty()) "Drag a field here to start your form" else "Drop here to add at the end")
}

The complete implementation is in the sample app: FormBuilderScreen.kt.

docs.title: Free-Form Placement (Sticky Notes)
docs.text:
Reordering and Kanban both move items between fixed slots. Some boards have no slots at all -- a note can land anywhere. This guide walks through the pattern used by the Sticky Notes Board sample: a free-form canvas where notes carry an absolute Offset position instead of a place in a list.

The building blocks:

  • Notes are plain draggableItems at an absolute position (Modifier.offset { ... }), not reorderableItems -- there is no list order to maintain.
  • The board itself is one big dropTarget, with dropAlignment = Alignment.TopStart and a dropOffset recomputed every frame from the dragged note's dragAmount, so the drop animation lands the ghost exactly on the snapped grid position.
  • A trash target overlaps the board with a higher zIndex, so it wins the hover check whenever the pointer is over both.

docs.title: Notes as Absolute-Position draggableItems
docs.text:
Each note stores its own top-left Offset and is positioned with Modifier.offset, then made draggable:

notes.forEach { note ->
    StickyNote(
        note = note,
        modifier = Modifier
            .offset { IntOffset(note.position.x.roundToInt(), note.position.y.roundToInt()) }
            .graphicsLayer { alpha = if (state.isDragging(note.id)) 0f else 1f }
            .draggableItem(
                key = note.id,
                data = note.id,
                state = state,
                draggableContent = {
                    StickyNote(note = note, isLifted = true)
                },
            ),
    )
}

Nothing here is specific to free-form placement yet -- it is the same hide-the-original-while-dragging pattern used everywhere else. The free-form part is entirely in how the board, as a drop target, computes where the note should land.

docs.title: The Board as One Drop Target, with a Live dropOffset
docs.text:
The board is a single dropTarget the size of the whole canvas. Its dropOffset is not a constant: it is recalculated on every recomposition from the position of the note currently being dragged, snapped to the grid:

fun landingPosition(note: Note, dragAmount: Offset): Offset {
    val moved = note.position + dragAmount
    val snapped = if (snapToGrid) {
        Offset(
            x = (moved.x / gridStepPx).roundToInt() * gridStepPx,
            y = (moved.y / gridStepPx).roundToInt() * gridStepPx,
        )
    } else {
        moved
    }
    return Offset(
        x = snapped.x.coerceIn(0f, (boardSize.width - noteSizePx).coerceAtLeast(0f)),
        y = snapped.y.coerceIn(0f, (boardSize.height - noteSizePx).coerceAtLeast(0f)),
    )
}

val draggedNote = state.draggedItem?.let { dragged -> notes.find { it.id == dragged.data } }
val landing = draggedNote?.let { note ->
    landingPosition(note, state.draggedItem?.dragAmount ?: Offset.Zero)
}

Box(
    modifier = Modifier
        .dropTarget(
            key = BOARD_KEY,
            state = state,
            dropAlignment = Alignment.TopStart,
            // Land the drop animation exactly on the snapped position
            dropOffset = landing ?: Offset.Zero,
            onDrop = { dragged ->
                onNotesChange(
                    notes.map { note ->
                        if (note.id == dragged.data) {
                            note.copy(position = landingPosition(note, dragged.dragAmount))
                        } else {
                            note
                        }
                    },
                )
            },
        ),
) {
    // grid dots, notes, trash target...
}

Why this works: dropAlignment = Alignment.TopStart makes the target's alignment contribute no offset of its own, so the final drop position is simply the target's own top-left plus dropOffset. Since the board is the target, that reduces to dropOffset alone, in the board's local coordinate space -- the same space note.position lives in. Setting dropOffset to the live, snapped landing position on every frame means that whenever the drag ends, the drop animation already knows the exact snapped square to animate the ghost into, instead of animating to the raw pointer position and jumping to the grid afterwards.

onDrop then repeats the same landingPosition calculation to commit the final position into state -- using the same function for the live preview and the committed value keeps them in sync by construction.

Tip

Showing a live preview of the landing square is a couple of lines once landing is computed: draw a dashed box at landing while state.isDropTargetHovered(BOARD_KEY) is true.

docs.title: A Trash Target That Wins on Overlap
docs.text:
The trash icon sits in a corner, visually overlapping the board. Both are drop targets that could receive the drop, so the trash target sets a higher zIndex to take priority whenever the two overlap:

TrashTarget(
    isVisible = state.draggedItem != null,
    isHovered = state.isDropTargetHovered(TRASH_TARGET_KEY),
    modifier = Modifier
        .align(Alignment.BottomEnd)
        .padding(16.dp)
        .dropTarget(
            key = TRASH_TARGET_KEY,
            state = state,
            // Wins over the board it overlaps
            zIndex = 1f,
            onDrop = { dragged ->
                onNotesChange(notes.filterNot { it.id == dragged.data })
            },
        ),
)

The board itself is left at the default zIndex = 0f. See Drop Strategies: Z-Index for how overlapping targets are resolved in general.

docs.title: Toggling Snap-to-Grid
docs.text:
snapToGrid is a plain boolean read inside landingPosition, so toggling it with a FilterChip changes both the live preview and the committed position on the very next frame -- no extra plumbing needed, since both paths already go through the same function.

The complete implementation is in the sample app: StickyNotesBoardScreen.kt.

docs.title: Multiple Lists (Kanban)
docs.text:
A Kanban board combines several features into a single screen: multiple columns, cross-column card transfer, positional insertion, auto-scroll on both axes, and reordering the columns themselves. This guide walks through the pattern used by the Kanban Board sample.

The building blocks:

  • One shared DragAndDropState for cards, so they can move between any columns.
  • A second DragAndDropState for the columns, dragged by their header. Two states let card drags and column drags coexist on one screen.
  • An outer LazyRow of columns and an inner LazyColumn per column, each with its own dragAutoScroll.
  • Modifier.reorderableItem on each card, handling both same-column reorder and cross-column insertion in a single callback.
  • A dropTarget under the cards of each column, so a card can be dropped below the last card or into an empty column.

On a narrow screen the board shows one column at a time. Holding a card or a column at the edge scrolls the board to the next ones:

docs.title: Data Model and State
docs.text:
Keep columns and cards in immutable state. A single state instance is shared across the whole board:

data class Card(val id: String, val title: String)

data class Column(val id: String, val title: String, val cards: List<Card>)

val dndState = rememberDragAndDropState<Card>()
var columns by remember { mutableStateOf(initialColumns()) }

docs.title: Board Layout
docs.text:
Wrap the board in one DragAndDropContainer. The outer LazyRow scrolls horizontally between columns while a card is dragged toward the screen edge; each column's LazyColumn scrolls vertically:

@Composable
fun KanbanBoard() {
    val dndState = rememberDragAndDropState<Card>()
    var columns by remember { mutableStateOf(initialColumns()) }
    val rowState = rememberLazyListState()

    DragAndDropContainer(state = dndState) {
        LazyRow(
            state = rowState,
            horizontalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(12.dp),
            modifier = Modifier
                .fillMaxSize()
                .dragAutoScroll(
                    state = dndState,
                    lazyListState = rowState,
                ),
        ) {
            items(columns, key = { it.id }) { column ->
                ColumnUi(
                    column = column,
                    dndState = dndState,
                    onReorder = { dragged, target ->
                        columns = columns.moveCard(dragged, target)
                    },
                    onDropInEmpty = { dragged ->
                        columns = columns.moveCardToColumn(dragged, column.id)
                    },
                )
            }
        }
    }
}

docs.title: Cards with reorderableItem
docs.text:
Each card uses the reorderableItem modifier. Because every card in every column shares the same state, dragging a card over a card in another column fires onDragEnter there — cross-column transfer works with the same callback as same-column reorder:

@Composable
fun ColumnUi(
    column: Column,
    dndState: DragAndDropState<Card>,
    onReorder: (dragged: Card, target: Card) -> Unit,
    onDropInEmpty: (dragged: Card) -> Unit,
) {
    val colState = rememberLazyListState()

    LazyColumn(
        state = colState,
        verticalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(8.dp),
        modifier = Modifier
            .width(280.dp)
            .dragAutoScroll(
                state = dndState,
                lazyListState = colState,
            ),
    ) {
        items(column.cards, key = { it.id }) { card ->
            val isDragging = dndState.isDragging(card.id)

            CardUi(
                card = card,
                modifier = Modifier
                    .animateItem()
                    .graphicsLayer { alpha = if (isDragging) 0f else 1f }
                    .reorderableItem(
                        key = card.id,
                        data = card,
                        state = dndState,
                        dropStrategy = DropStrategy.CenterDistance,
                        dragAfterLongPress = true,
                        onDragEnter = { state -> onReorder(state.data, card) },
                        draggableContent = {
                            CardUi(card = card, isDragShadow = true)
                        },
                    )
                    .fillMaxWidth(),
            )
        }
    }
}

Two choices matter here:

  • dropStrategy = DropStrategy.CenterDistance picks the closest card when the dragged card reaches several at once, e.g. on its way into another column. See Drop Strategies.
  • dragAfterLongPress = true keeps normal touch scrolling working — a plain swipe scrolls the column, a long press picks up the card.

docs.title: Cross-Column Move Logic
docs.text:
The reorder callback removes the dragged card from whichever column holds it and inserts it before the target card. One immutable transformation handles both same-column and cross-column moves:

fun List<Column>.moveCard(dragged: Card, target: Card): List<Column> {
    if (dragged.id == target.id) return this

    return map { col ->
        val targetIndex = col.cards.indexOfFirst { it.id == target.id }
        if (targetIndex == -1) {
            // Not the target column: just remove the dragged card if present
            col.copy(cards = col.cards.filter { it.id != dragged.id })
        } else {
            // Target column: remove then insert at the target position
            col.copy(
                cards = col.cards
                    .filter { it.id != dragged.id }
                    .toMutableList()
                    .apply { add(targetIndex.coerceAtMost(size), dragged) },
            )
        }
    }
}

Two lists are the smallest version of the same idea. Here a person either joins the end of the other team, or lands on the row they are dropped on:

docs.title: Dropping at the End of a Column
docs.text:
Cards only react when another card is under the dragged one. The empty area below the last card, and a column with no cards at all, need a target of their own. Make the whole list a dropTarget that sits under its cards:

LazyColumn(
    state = listState,
    modifier = Modifier
        .fillMaxSize()
        .dropTarget(
            key = "end-${column.id}",
            state = dndState,
            zIndex = -1f,
            dropAlignment = Alignment.TopStart,
            dropOffset = Offset(0f, lastSlotTop.toFloat()),
            onDragEnter = { state -> onCardEnterEnd(state.data) },
        )
        .dragAutoScroll(state = dndState, lazyListState = listState),
) {
    // cards
}

fun moveCardToEnd(card: Card, columnId: String) {
    columns = columns.map { column ->
        val rest = column.cards.filter { it.id != card.id }
        column.copy(cards = if (column.id == columnId) rest + card else rest)
    }
}
  • zIndex = -1f puts the list below its cards: when both are under the dragged card, only the cards are considered. The list gets the card when no card does.
  • onDragEnter moves the card to the end right away, like the cards do, so its slot opens while the card is still held.
  • dropAlignment and dropOffset aim the drop animation at that slot instead of the middle of the list. lastSlotTop is the offset of the last visible item:
val lastSlotTop by remember {
    derivedStateOf { listState.layoutInfo.visibleItemsInfo.lastOrNull()?.offset ?: 0 }
}

docs.title: Reordering the Columns Themselves
docs.text:
Columns are draggable too, by their header. The trick is a second DragAndDropState typed to columns, with its own container wrapped around the card container — each drag layer tracks its own items and renders its own shadow:

val cardDndState = rememberDragAndDropState<Card>()
val columnDndState = rememberDragAndDropState<Column>()

DragAndDropContainer(state = columnDndState) {
    DragAndDropContainer(state = cardDndState) {
        LazyRow(
            modifier = Modifier
                .dragAutoScroll(state = cardDndState, lazyListState = rowState)
                .dragAutoScroll(state = columnDndState, lazyListState = rowState),
        ) {
            // columns...
        }
    }
}

Each column becomes a reorderableItem in the column state, with hasDragHandle = true so that only the header initiates the drag — otherwise every card gesture would also grab the column:

Column(
    modifier = Modifier
        .graphicsLayer { alpha = if (isColumnDragging) 0f else 1f }
        .reorderableItem(
            key = "col-${column.id}",
            data = column,
            state = columnDndState,
            hasDragHandle = true,
            dragAxis = DragAxis.Horizontal,
            dropStrategy = DropStrategy.CenterDistance,
            onDragEnter = { state -> onColumnEnter(state.data, column) },
            draggableContent = { ColumnDragPreview(column) },
        ),
) {
    Row(
        modifier = Modifier
            .fillMaxWidth()
            .dragHandle(
                key = "col-${column.id}",
                state = columnDndState,
            ),
    ) {
        // header content: colored dot, title, count, grip dots
    }

    // cards LazyColumn...
}

Useful details:

  • dragAxis = DragAxis.Horizontal keeps the lifted column aligned with the row.
  • The column reorder callback moves the column by id, mirroring the card logic.
  • draggableContent renders a simplified preview (header plus the first few cards) instead of the full live column, keeping the drag shadow cheap.

Tip

Cards of different heights swap without bouncing: a card takes the slot of another one when its leading edge passes the middle of that card, whatever their sizes — see Reorder List.

The complete implementation, including priorities, tags, and assignees on the cards, is in the sample app: KanbanBoardScreen.kt.

docs.title: Drag to Select and Multi-Select
docs.text:
Some interactions need one draggable item to drive two different gestures depending on how the drag starts. This guide walks through the pattern used by the Photo Gallery sample, a grid where the same photo tile supports:

  • Drag to select -- long-press an unselected photo and drag across the grid to select a range, like Google Photos.
  • Group drag -- long-press an already-selected photo to drag the whole selection as a stack onto an album.

Both gestures reuse the same draggableItem; the mode is picked in onDragStart, based on whether the pressed photo was already selected.

The building blocks:

  • One DragAndDropState<Int> where the dragged data is a single photo id -- the anchor of the gesture, not necessarily everything that moves.
  • Every photo tile is both a draggableItem and a dropTarget, so a dragged photo entering another tile can extend the selection.
  • onDragStart decides the mode; draggableContent renders different content (or nothing) depending on it.
  • Selection state (Set<Int>) lives outside the drag payload, so a group drag can move more items than the single id carried by the drag.

docs.title: Picking the Mode in onDragStart
docs.text:
private enum class GalleryDragMode { None, Select, Move }

fun onDragStart(id: Int) {
    anchorId = id
    if (id in selection) {
        dragMode = GalleryDragMode.Move
    } else {
        dragMode = GalleryDragMode.Select
        baseSelection = selection
        selection = selection + id
    }
}

onDragStart fires once, before the pointer has moved, so it is the right place to branch: dragging a photo that is not selected starts a fresh range selection (and selects it immediately); dragging one that is selected picks up the whole selection as a group.

docs.title: Drag to Select
docs.text:
Each photo is a draggableItem with no drag shadow in select mode -- the pointer just extends the selection as it passes over tiles -- and a dropTarget that only accepts drags while selecting:

PhotoTile(
    photo = photo,
    isSelected = isSelected,
    modifier = Modifier
        .draggableItem(
            key = photo.id,
            data = photo.id,
            state = state,
            dropStrategy = DropStrategy.CenterDistance,
            onDragStart = { gallery.onDragStart(it.data) },
            onDragEnd = { gallery.onDragEnd() },
            draggableContent = {
                // Drag-select has no shadow, only a group drag shows one
                if (gallery.dragMode == GalleryDragMode.Move) {
                    SelectionStack(photos = gallery.photos.filter { it.id in gallery.selection })
                }
            },
        ).dropTarget(
            key = photo.id,
            state = state,
            canDrop = gallery.dragMode == GalleryDragMode.Select,
            dropAnimationEnabled = false,
            onDragEnter = { gallery.extendSelectionTo(photo.id) },
        ),
)
  • canDrop = gallery.dragMode == GalleryDragMode.Select keeps the tile out of hover detection during a group drag, so photos don't re-select themselves while being carried to an album. See Conditional Drop.
  • dropAnimationEnabled = false matters here because this target is only ever used for the live range extension in onDragEnter -- there is no meaningful "drop" on a photo tile.
  • dropStrategy = DropStrategy.CenterDistance picks the tile whose center is closest to the dragged photo, which behaves well for equally sized grid cells. See Drop Strategies.
  • onDragEnter calls extendSelectionTo, which selects every photo between the anchor and the entered tile:
fun extendSelectionTo(id: Int) {
    if (dragMode != GalleryDragMode.Select) return
    val anchorIndex = photos.indexOfFirst { it.id == anchorId }
    val index = photos.indexOfFirst { it.id == id }
    if (anchorIndex == -1 || index == -1) return

    val range = photos.subList(minOf(anchorIndex, index), maxOf(anchorIndex, index) + 1)
    selection = baseSelection + range.map { it.id }
}

Because baseSelection snapshots the selection before the drag started, dragging back and forth shrinks and grows the range instead of accumulating leftover selections.

docs.title: Group Drag
docs.text:
When the pressed photo is already selected, dragMode becomes Move and draggableContent renders a fanned stack of the selected photos with a count badge, instead of nothing:

@Composable
private fun SelectionStack(photos: List<Photo>) {
    Box(modifier = Modifier.size(96.dp)) {
        photos.takeLast(3).forEachIndexed { index, photo ->
            PhotoArt(
                photo = photo,
                modifier = Modifier
                    .size(80.dp)
                    .align(Alignment.Center)
                    .graphicsLayer { rotationZ = (index - 1) * 8f }
                    .shadow(8.dp, RoundedCornerShape(8.dp)),
            )
        }
        // count badge in the corner...
    }
}

The album row is a plain dropTarget per album. Note that onDrop moves gallery.selection, not state.data -- the drag only ever carries the one id it started on, but the whole selection is what the group drag represents:

AlbumChip(
    album = album,
    isHovered = state.isDropTargetHovered("album-${album.key}"),
    modifier = Modifier
        .weight(1f)
        .dropTarget(
            key = "album-${album.key}",
            state = state,
            canDrop = isMoving,
            onDrop = { onDropOnAlbum(album.key) },
        ),
)

fun moveSelectionTo(albumKey: String) {
    val moved = photos.filter { it.id in selection }
    photos = photos.filterNot { it.id in selection }
    albums = albums.map { album ->
        if (album.key == albumKey) album.copy(photos = album.photos + moved) else album
    }
    selection = emptySet()
}

This is the key idea for group drags: the library only ever drags one payload, but nothing stops your onDrop/onDragEnter handlers from acting on a larger piece of app state (the selection) that the dragged id merely represents.

docs.title: Suppressing Auto Scroll During a Group Drag
docs.text:
The gallery grid uses auto scroll while selecting, but disables it while carrying a group to an album, since the pointer is headed for the album row above the grid, not further into it:

LazyVerticalGrid(
    columns = GridCells.Adaptive(minSize = 96.dp),
    state = gridState,
    modifier = Modifier
        .weight(1f)
        .then(if (isMoving) Modifier else Modifier.dragAutoScroll(state, gridState)),
) {
    // photo tiles...
}

The complete implementation is in the sample app: PhotoGalleryScreen.kt.

docs.title: Drag and Drop Overview
docs.text:
Compose DND provides a declarative API for adding drag and drop functionality to your Compose UI. The core building blocks are:

  • DragAndDropState -- Holds the state for all drag and drop operations.
  • DragAndDropContainer -- A container that wraps all draggable items and drop targets.
  • draggableItem modifier -- Makes a composable draggable.
  • dropTarget modifier -- Marks a composable as a drop target.
  • DraggableItem composable -- A wrapper alternative to the draggableItem modifier (see the alternative section).

docs.title: Creating DragAndDropState
docs.text:
Use rememberDragAndDropState to create and remember a DragAndDropState instance. The type parameter T defines the type of data carried by dragged items.

val dragAndDropState = rememberDragAndDropState<String>()

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Default Description dragAfterLongPress Boolean false If true, drag starts after a long press. If false, drag starts on touch move. Applied to all items unless overridden per item. requireFirstDownUnconsumed Boolean false If true, the first down pointer event must be unconsumed to initiate drag. reorderHysteresisDistance Dp DefaultReorderHysteresisDistance (8.dp) How far the drag must come back after a reorder swap before that swap is undone. See Reorder List.

docs.title: DragAndDropContainer
docs.text:
All draggable items and drop targets must be placed inside a DragAndDropContainer. This composable handles pointer input tracking and renders the drag shadow.

DragAndDropContainer(
    state = dragAndDropState,
    modifier = Modifier.fillMaxSize(),
    enabled = true,
) {
    // Draggable items and drop targets go here
}

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Default Description state DragAndDropState<T> Required The drag and drop state. modifier Modifier Modifier Modifier for the container. enabled Boolean true Whether drag and drop is enabled. content @Composable () -> Unit Required The content of the container.

docs.title: Making Items Draggable
docs.text:
Apply the Modifier.draggableItem modifier to any composable. Each item needs a unique key, the data to pass to the drop target when dropped, and a draggableContent that is rendered as the drag shadow:

val isDragging = dragAndDropState.isDragging("item-1")

Text(
    text = "Drag me",
    modifier = Modifier
        .graphicsLayer { alpha = if (isDragging) 0f else 1f }
        .draggableItem(
            key = "item-1",
            data = "Hello World",
            state = dragAndDropState,
            draggableContent = {
                Text("Drag me") // Content shown as the drag shadow
            },
        ),
)

Use DragAndDropState.isDragging(key) to check if a specific item is being dragged - hiding the original with graphicsLayer { alpha = ... } while the shadow follows the pointer is the usual pattern.

The item's configuration (dropTargets, dropStrategy, dragAxis, dropAnimationSpec, draggableContent) is captured when a drag starts and applies for that whole drag, even if the composable recomposes with different values while dragging.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Default Description key Any Required Unique key identifying this item. data T Required Data passed to the drop target on drop. state DragAndDropState<T> Required The drag and drop state. enabled Boolean true Whether this specific item is draggable. dragAfterLongPress Boolean Inherits from state Override the long-press drag behavior for this item. requireFirstDownUnconsumed Boolean Inherits from state Override the unconsumed pointer requirement for this item. dropTargets List<Any> emptyList() Restrict which drop targets this item can be dropped on. Empty means any target. dropStrategy DropStrategy DropStrategy.Surface Strategy for choosing the hovered drop target. dragAxis DragAxis DragAxis.Free Constrain drag movement to one axis. See Axis Lock. hasDragHandle Boolean false If true, drag is initiated from a dragHandle modifier instead of the whole item. See Drag Handle. dropAnimationSpec AnimationSpec<Offset> SpringSpec() Animation for position when dropping. onDragStart (DraggedItemState<T>) -> Unit {} Called when a drag of this item starts. onDragEnd (DraggedItemState<T>) -> Unit {} Called once the drag of this item is over. See Drag Lifecycle. draggableContent @Composable () -> Unit Required Content rendered as the drag shadow while dragging.

docs.title: Drag Lifecycle: onDragStart and onDragEnd
docs.text:
draggableItem, reorderableItem, DraggableItem and ReorderableItem all accept onDragStart and onDragEnd callbacks, both (DraggedItemState<T>) -> Unit:

Text(
    text = "Drag me",
    modifier = Modifier.draggableItem(
        key = "item-1",
        data = "Hello",
        state = dragAndDropState,
        onDragStart = { state -> println("Started dragging ${state.data}") },
        onDragEnd = { state -> println("Drag of ${state.data} is over") },
        draggableContent = {
            Text("Drag me")
        },
    ),
)
  • onDragStart fires once, when the drag begins.
  • onDragEnd fires once per drag, after the drag is fully over: for a successful drop, that's after the drop target's onDrop and once the drop animation lands on the target; for a cancelled drag (see cancelDrag) or a release outside any target, it's after the return animation. This makes it a reliable place to persist state -- it runs exactly once per drag, unlike onDragEnter which can fire many times. See Reorder List: Persisting the new order for an example.

docs.title: Drop Target
docs.text:
Use the Modifier.dropTarget extension to mark any composable as a drop target.

Box(
    modifier = Modifier
        .size(200.dp)
        .dropTarget(
            key = "target-1",
            state = dragAndDropState,
            onDrop = { state ->
                println("Dropped item: ${state.data}")
            },
            onDragEnter = { state ->
                println("Item entered: ${state.data}")
            },
            onDragExit = { state ->
                println("Item exited: ${state.data}")
            },
        )
) {
    Text("Drop here")
}

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Default Description key Any Required Unique key identifying this drop target. state DragAndDropState<T> Required The drag and drop state. zIndex Float 0f Z-index for overlapping targets. Higher values take priority. dropAlignment Alignment Alignment.Center Alignment of the dropped item within the target for the drop animation. dropOffset Offset Offset.Zero Additional offset for the drop animation position. dropAnimationEnabled Boolean true Whether to animate the drop. If false, the drop callback fires immediately. canDrop Boolean true Whether this target accepts drops. When false, dragged items cannot hover over or be dropped on this target. Can read state.draggedItem?.data to validate dynamically. onDrop (DraggedItemState<T>) -> Unit {} Called when an item is dropped on this target. See onDrop timing below. onDragEnter (DraggedItemState<T>) -> Unit {} Called when a dragged item enters this target. onDragExit (DraggedItemState<T>) -> Unit {} Called when a dragged item exits this target.

docs.title: onDrop Timing
docs.text:
onDrop is called once the drop animation has landed the drag shadow on the target, right before the dragged item's onDragEnd. With dropAnimationEnabled = false it is called immediately, as soon as the item is released -- there is no animation to wait for.

If you mutate your list inside onDrop, keep that in mind when the animation is enabled: the visual drop and the state change happen together, which is usually what you want. For a callback that always fires exactly once per drag regardless of where it landed, use the item's onDragEnd instead (see Drag Lifecycle above).

docs.title: DraggedItemState
docs.text:
The callbacks receive a DraggedItemState<T> with the following properties:

  • key: Any -- The key of the dragged item.
  • data: T -- The data associated with the dragged item.
  • dragAmount: Offset -- The total drag offset from the original position.

docs.title: Container Level
docs.text:
Disable drag and drop for all items within a container:

DragAndDropContainer(
    state = dragAndDropState,
    enabled = false, // Disables all drag and drop
) {
    // ...
}

docs.title: Item Level
docs.text:
Disable drag and drop for a specific item by passing enabled = false to the draggableItem modifier:

Text(
    text = "Cannot drag me",
    modifier = Modifier.draggableItem(
        key = "item-1",
        data = "Hello",
        state = dragAndDropState,
        enabled = false, // Only this item is disabled
        draggableContent = { Text("Cannot drag me") },
    ),
)

docs.title: Observing Drag State
docs.text:
Use DragAndDropState.isDropTargetHovered(key) to check whether a specific drop target is currently hovered by the dragged item:

val isHovered = dragAndDropState.isDropTargetHovered("target-1")

Box(
    modifier = Modifier
        .border(
            width = 2.dp,
            color = if (isHovered) Color.Blue else Color.Gray,
        )
        .dropTarget(
            key = "target-1",
            state = dragAndDropState,
            onDrop = { /* ... */ },
        )
) {
    Text("Drop here")
}

isDropTargetHovered(key) is equivalent to hoveredDropTargetKey == key; hoveredDropTargetKey is still there directly on the state if you need the raw key, for example to look it up in a map.

You can also check if any item is being dragged using DragAndDropState.draggedItem:

val isDragging = dragAndDropState.draggedItem != null

docs.title: Cancelling a Drag Programmatically
docs.text:
DragAndDropState.cancelDrag() aborts the drag in progress, if any: the drag shadow animates back to the dragged item, no drop target receives onDrop, the hovered target (if any) gets its onDragExit, and the item's onDragEnd fires once the return animation ends. It does nothing when no drag is in progress or the item was already released.

This is useful to abort a drag on a back press, an Escape key, or when the dragged data becomes invalid mid-drag:

BackHandler(enabled = dragAndDropState.draggedItem != null) {
    dragAndDropState.cancelDrag()
}

Disabling a DragAndDropContainer (enabled = false) while a drag is in progress also calls cancelDrag() internally, so the drag never gets stuck. A gesture canceled by the system is canceled the same way.

docs.title: Full Working Example
docs.text:
@Composable
fun DragAndDropExample() {
    val dragAndDropState = rememberDragAndDropState<Int>()
    var isDropped by remember { mutableStateOf(false) }

    DragAndDropContainer(
        state = dragAndDropState,
        modifier = Modifier.fillMaxSize(),
    ) {
        Column(
            verticalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(20.dp),
            modifier = Modifier.fillMaxSize().padding(20.dp),
        ) {
            // Source area
            Box(
                contentAlignment = Alignment.Center,
                modifier = Modifier
                    .fillMaxWidth()
                    .weight(1f)
                    .border(1.dp, Color.Gray, RoundedCornerShape(16.dp)),
            ) {
                if (!isDropped) {
                    val isDragging = dragAndDropState.isDragging(1)

                    RedBox(
                        text = "Drag me",
                        modifier = Modifier
                            .graphicsLayer {
                                alpha = if (isDragging) 0f else 1f
                            }
                            .draggableItem(
                                key = 1,
